metaDescription: How Techlio works: a five-stage process, three engagement paths from advisory to end-to-end delivery, and the release discipline behind every build.
heroTitle: You always know what happens next, and who owns it.
heroIntro: One process for every engagement, whether we advise, build alongside your team or deliver the whole product.
pathsTitle: Three ways to work with us
pathsIntro: Each path includes the one before it. Many clients start with advisory and move right as trust builds.

paths.name: Advisory and architecture
paths.text: Senior engineers review your stack, rank the opportunities and design the system. Your team, or any vendor, builds from the result.
paths.fit: Teams with engineers but no AI track record
paths.model: Fixed price or time and material

paths.name: Co-build with embedded engineers
paths.text: A senior Techlio pod joins your standups, repositories and release process. You keep direction and ownership; we add capacity and AI depth.
paths.fit: Teams with a roadmap and not enough senior hands

paths.name: End-to-end product delivery
paths.line: We own it from scope to production.
paths.text: Design, engineering, QA, cloud, security and launch from one accountable team, against a statement of work agreed before any code is written.
paths.fit: Founders and business units without an engineering team
paths.model: Fixed price against a detailed scope

pathsNote: Day to day we work in the tools you already use, including Slack, Jira, Trello and Asana.
phaseAIntro: Three steps, in order. Nothing is built until you have approved the output of the third.

phaseA.title: Specification
phaseA.text: We turn goals into a written scope with users, workflows, constraints and a success measure.
list: Review of code, infrastructure and data

phaseA.title: Design and prototype
phaseA.text: Architecture and UI/UX are designed together, with a clickable prototype for anything users will touch.

phaseA.title: Estimate and timeline
phaseA.text: A proposal with scope, milestones, team and price, including the assumptions behind each number.

phaseBIntro: Five steps, in order, repeated in weekly cycles until launch.

phaseB.title: Prepare the data
phaseB.text: Sources connected, cleaned and permissioned. The eval set is assembled from real cases.

phaseB.title: Prove the approach
phaseB.text: Models, prompts and retrieval strategies are compared on the eval set before one is chosen.

phaseB.title: Build and test
phaseB.text: Features ship weekly to staging with automated tests, evals, security checks and senior review on every change.

phaseB.title: Deploy and integrate
phaseB.text: Canary rollout to production, connected to your systems, with rollback ready.

phaseB.title: Monitor and improve
phaseB.text: Quality, cost and latency are tracked. Production failures become new eval cases.

buildIntro: The same pipeline applies to code, prompts and model upgrades. Run both traces to see what happens when a change makes things worse.

principles.title: Evals over guesswork
principles.text: Answer quality is a number tracked per release, built from your own cases, not a feeling from a demo.

principles.title: Strict multi-tenant security
principles.text: Isolation is enforced in the database and proven by tests that try to break it on every change.

principles.title: Human-in-the-loop guardrails
principles.text: High-impact and low-confidence actions wait for a person. Thresholds are set from evidence.

principles.title: Senior-led execution
principles.text: A senior engineer scopes, leads and reviews. The person you meet on the first call stays on the work.

closeText: Thirty minutes with a senior engineer is enough to pick a path and outline the first milestone.
